Lessons.Title: Partial Products and the Standard Algorithm
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will analyze the standard algorithm for multiplication and compare it to an algorithm that uses partial products you saw in earlier lessons.
In previous lessons, you analyzed and used an algorithm that uses partial products to multiply multi-digit whole numbers. You learned that an algorithm can represent the base-ten diagrams and rectangular diagrams, but it is more efficient for keeping track of and recording partial products. This lesson extends your analysis to include the standard algorithm for multiplication of multi-digit numbers.
Core relationship: Relate partial products to the standard algorithm. Connect each partial product to its place-value meaning in the standard layout.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Number Talk: The Value of the Digits	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Two Algorithms to Multiply	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Algorithm Comparison	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Choose a Way to Multiply	 (5 minutes)
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
